questions.explanation: Important Features of National Population Policy, 2000.  The NPP reinforces the Government's vision of encouraging voluntary and informed choices and consent of citizens to derive maximum benefits from reproductive health services.  Making school education free and compulsory up to the age of 14 and reducing school dropout rates for both boys and girls.  Reducing the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in the country to less than 30 per 1000 live births (this was to be achieved by 2010 when the NPP was introduced).  Reducing Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) to less than 100 per 1 lakh live births (this was to be achieved by 2010 as scheduled when NPP was introduced).  To achieve universal immunization of all children against vaccine-preventable diseases.  Encouraging delayed marriage for girls (preferably before 18 years and above 20 years). 80 percent institutional deliveries and 100 percent deliveries by trained persons.  To achieve 100% registration of pregnancies, births, deaths and marriages.  To provide universal access to information/counseling and services for reproductive regulation and contraception with a wide range of options.  Preventing the spread of AIDS, promoting better coordination between the management of reproductive tract infections (RTIs) and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and the National AIDS Control Organization (NACO).  Prevention and control of communicable diseases. Integrating Indian systems of medicine (AYUSH) into reproductive and child health services.  The ideal of small family is being vigorously pursued. To bring about integration of all related social programs so that family planning and welfare becomes a people-centred programme. The NPP 2000 differs from previous population regulation programs in that for the first time the population problem was linked with child survival, maternal health, women empowerment and contraception issues.
